provenance.instrument: Borough of Chambersburg Code Chapter 300 Zoning (Ord. No. 82-7, 6-23-1982, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2026-09-28 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 2026-07 (Ch 135, electric) and 2026-08 (Ch 286, vehicles), neither zoning.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2026-09-28'. The two New Laws (2026-10-26) do not amend Chapter 300.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment, in-law, ECHO or granny flat provision. A code search for those words and for cottage, 'accessory unit' and 'living quarters' found only watchman or caretaker quarters in the manufacturing districts (300-50, 300-55)

A two-family dwelling is permitted by right in LDR (6,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, so 12,000 for two) and MDR (3,600 per unit, so 7,200), and through them in DCN, DCH, Central Core, Professional Office, Health Care Service and Health Institution (625 sq ft per family in a building for two or more families where stated) (300-14C, 300-17C, 300-23, 300-26, 300-31A, 300-35A, 300-36A, 300-40A, 300-44, 300-70A, 300-73D, 300-146Y, 300-155J)

Conversion apartments: the Zoning Hearing Board may allow, by special exception, the conversion of a building that existed on 6-23-1982 into a dwelling for two or more families in a residential district. Lot area per family at least 6,000 sq ft in LDR and 625 sq ft in other residential districts. No outside structural change except for sanitation or safety. Only for 'a large building which has relatively little economic value or usefulness as a conforming dwelling' (300-135, 300-24A)
Where neither public sewer nor public water is provided, each lot needs 20,000 sq ft per family. With one of them, 10,000 sq ft per family (300-133C(1))
Parking: 2 spaces 'per each family or dwelling' (300-77A). In the Southgate Neighborhood Overlay half of that (300-61A). None in Central Core (300-45)

An accessory building (a garage attached to a one-family house, or a detached building of the same design used for an accessory use) may project into the required rear yard. Such a projection may occupy at most 35% of the required rear yard, be at most 15 ft high and at least 6 ft from the rear lot line, and a detached one must be at least 60 ft from the front lot line (300-133E(1)). Outside the required rear yard the district height applies
In LDR every dwelling must have at least 900 sq ft of floor area, not counting a basement (300-20)
A group housing development (two or more buildings on a plot of at least five acres that is not subdivided) is a special exception in LDR and MDR (300-15C, 300-24C, 300-136)
The subdivision of an existing attached or semidetached dwelling or accessory structure may be allowed by special exception, outside the manufacturing districts (300-138.4)
Recreational vehicles may not be used as a dwelling while parked or stored on a lot (300-76E)

LDR, MDR, DCN, Central Core and Professional Office also permit 'uses which are of the same general character' as the listed uses (300-14N, 300-23F, 300-31M, 300-40D, 300-70I). Whether a second unit on a house lot could qualify is for the Zoning Officer. It is not an ADU rule
A boardinghouse may not use accessory buildings or garages as living units (300-138.1D)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Chambersburg Land Use and Community Development. Read on eCode360 (CH1151) in a browser, one print view at a time, on 2026-11-14. Use lists read for LDR, MDR, DCN, DCH, Central Core, Southgate Neighborhood Overlay and Professional Office. The Health Care Service and Health Institution use lists were not read, and the code searches found no ADU-like listing there.

term.note: No ADU term. Code searches for 'accessory dwelling', 'accessory apartment', 'in-law', ECHO, granny, caretaker, cottage, 'accessory unit' and 'living quarters' found no ADU text (2026-11-14).

status.note: The code has no ADU text.

path.note: A second dwelling unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use. It needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). A two-family dwelling is permitted by right in LDR and MDR, so a unit could be added as a conversion to a two-family dwelling if the lot meets the per-unit lot area, and conversion apartments are a special exception (300-135).

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family dwelling, with public sewer and water
value.conditions: A building for two families living independently of each other. Lot area per dwelling unit: LDR 6,000, MDR 3,600 (lot coverage 30%), and 625 sq ft per family in DCH, Central Core and Professional Office. Two parking spaces per family. Without public sewer and water, 20,000 sq ft per family (10,000 with one of them).
value.note: Read as a path for an existing house converted to two units. DCN dwellings follow the MDR area rules (300-32). Professional Office lots need 6,000 sq ft for a detached building (300-73D). Health Care Service allows the Professional Office uses (300-146Y) and Health Institution the LDR and Professional Office residential uses (300-155J). No lot area figure for a dwelling is set in those two districts.

value.name: Two-family dwelling, without public sewer or public water
value.conditions: Where neither public sewer nor public water is provided, 20,000 sq ft per family, so 40,000 for two, and 100 ft width. With one of them, 10,000 per family, so 20,000 for two, and 75 ft width.
value.note: The 40,000 figure is for a lot with neither service. A lot with one of them needs 20,000.

value.name: Conversion apartments
value.conditions: Conversion of a building that existed when the chapter took effect into a dwelling for two or more families. 6,000 sq ft of lot per family in LDR, 625 in other residential districts. Yards, building area and parking may not be reduced. No outside structural change except for sanitation or safety. Only for a large building with little economic value or use as a conforming dwelling.

requires.condition: The building existed at the effective date of the chapter (adopted 6-23-1982)
A large building with relatively little economic value or usefulness as a conforming dwelling

value.note: MDR lists conversion apartments as a special exception (300-24A). 300-135 names 'any residential district', so LDR is included. The adoption date of the chapter is used as its effective date. Without public sewer and water, 300-133C(1) sets 20,000 sq ft per family (10,000 with one of them).
